answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nonrefundable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits confirm fraud. Because identities that pass checks earn access gradually, a sybil attacker must fund every fake account and risk losing each deposit; multiplying names is no longer cheap. The bond need not be a quill, saffron, or relic: it can be a transferable token, provided audits are credible and honest agents can appeal mistakes.
